Hi Alex — great demo today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and the items we promised to follow up on so your team can evaluate feasibility with networking and security teams.

High-level ask: BridgeWorks would like to run inference from their prod VPC with private connectivity (no public egress) while using Redwood’s Dedicated offering. Key integration points we discussed: SDK setup, auth model, routing for model variants (cost vs latency), structured output/tool-calling, and embeddings + reranker flow for search relevance.

Action items (from Redwood):
- Share recommended SDK quickstart and minimal auth examples for VPC/private endpoints (we’ll attach the package).
- Provide IP allowlist / VPC endpoint CIDR ranges & expected egress behavior for model downloads and telemetry.
- Clarify mTLS and DNS requirements for mutual-auth p2p between BridgeWorks VPC and Redwood edge.
- Outline an embeddings + reranker architecture for post-processing (cost estimate + latency targets).

Questions for your infra/security folks (please loop them in if helpful):
1) Do you require full private peering (VPC peering/Transit) or are VPC endpoints with restricted egress sufficient?
2) Any existing egress proxy/inspection appliances that would break mTLS?
3) Preferred cert management (ACM, internal CA, HSM)?

Deliverables attached: short requirements PDF and the SDK quickstart. I’ll follow up internally and circle back with a target integration checklist and an estimate for Reserved capacity sizing.

Next step: Can we schedule a 45-min network deep-dive early next week with your infra and security (propose Mon/Tue)?

Cheers,
Diego
Senior Solutions Engineer

Thanks Diego — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying notes from our side before we bring infra/security into the loop: 

- Preference is to avoid VPC peering where possible. We prefer VPC endpoint (private link) style connectivity to limit blast radius.
- We use an egress proxy in prod that terminates TLS and applies DLP. That might interfere with mTLS unless we can route to a bypass path.
- Certs: we use an internal CA for service-to-service, but can accept external certs if pinned. HSM for keys is in scope for later phases.

Immediate asks from us:
1) If we use a VPC endpoint model, what inbound CIDR ranges or hostnames does Redwood require? Are there DNS names that must resolve to private IPs in our VPC?
2) Can you document the model artifact staging flow — where do model files come from (S3, OCI), how often are they pulled, and whether those pulls require public internet access?
3) For embeddings + reranker: what is the recommended approach for sending embeddings data (batched vs streaming), and do you support shipping only vectors (no raw text) for privacy?

Happy to set Monday 9am PT for a technical call — invite sent to Diego/Laura/our infra lead.

—Alex
CTO, BridgeWorks AI

Short answers / notes for consolidation:

1) CIDR / hostnames:
- For our private-link endpoint we publish a hostname per-region, e.g. private.redwood-inference.us-west-2.internal. We can provide an A record that resolves to the endpoint ENI in the customer's VPC via Private DNS. No broad CIDR list required if you use PrivateLink.
- If customer prefers IP allowlist, minimal set: 34.198.12.0/26, 34.198.13.0/26 (region-specific; will provide full list per-region).

2) Model staging flow:
- Model artifacts are stored in our secure artifact registry (S3-compatible behind customer-accessible VPC endpoints for Dedicated/private deployments). In dedicated/private mode, model pulls occur over the private connection. For hosted API clients that do not use PrivateLink, model downloads happen in our control plane and may traverse public network (we do not require customers to pull models).
- Frequency: models are downloaded on deploy + periodic health syncs (default 1 hour) and on cache misses for large artifacts.

3) Embeddings & reranker:
- Support both batched and streaming vector ingestion. For privacy we can accept precomputed vectors only (no raw text). We have a mode where vectors are uploaded via an HTTPS endpoint over PrivateLink — data never touches public internet.
- Reranker options: local rerank in their VPC (they send embeddings only + metadata) or use Redwood’s rerank service over PrivateLink. Latency targets: both feasible; local rerank reduces RTT but increases customer infra work.

mTLS + egress proxy note:
- If their egress proxy terminates TLS and performs inspection, it will break client-cert-based mTLS. Options: 1) Provide a bypass route for traffic to Redwood endpoints; 2) Terminate mTLS at an internal gateway and use an internal trust anchor to the egress proxy (complex); 3) Use private DNS + IP-level routing to avoid the proxy. We should ask for their proxy topology diagrams in the deep-dive.

I’ll draft a minimal checklist and the per-region hostnames/CIDRs before the call.

Ben

Alex — thanks for the quick answers. Below is a consolidated response and proposed agenda for Monday’s 9am PT call (invite sent). I’ve attached the checklist and SDK quickstart for your infra team to review ahead of time.

Consolidated technical notes (short):
- Connectivity model: PrivateLink (VPC endpoint) is the recommended path. We can publish a per-region private hostname that you can resolve in your VPC via AWS Private DNS. If you strongly prefer IP allowlists we will provide the minimal per-region CIDRs but PrivateLink avoids the need to manage those.
- Model artifact flow: In Dedicated/private deployments model artifacts are pulled over the private connection (no public egress). Model downloads occur on deploy + periodic syncs; they do not require manual customer pulls.
- Embeddings / rerank: We support precomputed vectors (upload-only) and vector-only ingestion over PrivateLink. Option A: you host the reranker in your VPC (we provide model + runtime recommendations). Option B: use Redwood rerank service over PrivateLink (simpler ops).
- mTLS vs egress proxy: Your proxy that terminates TLS will prevent client mTLS. Options to consider (we’ll walk through these on Monday): bypass path, internal gateway termination, or alternate routing to end-to-end mTLS.

Proposed Monday agenda (45m):
1) 5m — Introductions & scope
2) 10m — BridgeWorks infra/proxy topology (diagram)
3) 10m — PrivateLink hostnames / DNS / cert exchange plan
4) 10m — Embeddings + reranker flow (local vs Redwood) and performance expectations
5) 5m — Next steps & action owners (checklist review)

Prep for your team: please share a short network diagram and confirm whether a PrivateLink endpoint is acceptable; if not, confirm desire for IP allowlisting and we’ll send region CIDRs.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Diego
